newsitem.title: UK: Branson's Virgin launches personal pension product.
newsitem.headline: Branson's Virgin launches personal pension product.

text.p: Virgin Group, owned by British entrepreneur Richard Branson, is to extend its foray into the life assurance sector with personal pensions.
The company began selling simple low-cost life and health insurance products over the telephone in May and on Friday announced the launch of a personal pension product.
Virgin believes there is a need for cheap, easy to understand life and savings products in a market, which it says has become too complex for most customers.
"There is a huge gap between what consumers need and what the pensions industry has to offer," Branson said.
Virgin is to charge an annual management fee of one percent, which decreases to 0.7 percent, as the customer nears retirement and there will be a two stg flat fee for every payment made.
For years, the life assurance sector has been a bastion of commission-seeking middlemen and the big British insurers have only recently started experimenting with direct sales.

Some industry experts argue that pensions, income protection and health policies cannot be sold like car and household property cover. The individuals' demands differ too much and products must be specifically tailored, they say. Rowan Gormley, managing director of the Virgin Direct insurance business, said the company aimed to force the pensions industry out of its "complacency" with the new product.
"In terms of impact on the market, the impact will probably be quite disproportionate compared to the volumes we do, because existing products are opaque and charges are too high," he said.
"Now someone has set a standard for simple, straightforward low charges, there will be pressure to stand up to that."

Virgin plans to sell its pensions over the telephone. But it will not be cold-calling new customers, who it hopes will respond instead to advertising. Gormley said that Virgin would advise customers against switching out of occupational pensions.
